gloss: reading through; reading from cover to cover

definitions.gloss: reading through; reading from beginning to end
definitions.explanation: Reading a text, book, or document in its entirety from start to finish, as opposed to skimming, sampling, or reading selected portions.

examples.japanese: この{本|ほん}を{通読|つうどく}した。
examples.english: I read this book from cover to cover.

examples.japanese: {契約書|けいやくしょ}を{通読|つうどく}してからサインした。
examples.english: I read through the contract before signing it.

examples.japanese: {辞書|じしょ}を{最初|さいしょ}から{最後|さいご}まで{通読|つうどく}する{人|ひと}はめったにいない。
examples.english: Very few people read a dictionary from beginning to end.

notes:
Emphasizes completeness — reading every part of a text without skipping. Often used when describing a thorough or disciplined approach to reading.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {一気|いっき}に{通読|つうどく}する — to read through in one sitting
- {全巻|ぜんかん}{通読|つうどく} — reading through all volumes
- {通読|つうどく}に{値|あたい}する — worth reading through

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {精読|せいどく} — close reading, careful reading (focuses on depth of comprehension)
- {速読|そくどく} — speed reading (focuses on reading quickly)
- {多読|たどく} — extensive reading (reading large quantities)
- {拾|ひろ}い{読|よ}み — selective reading, reading bits and pieces (the opposite approach)
